ideas.description: Bank the E116 late freeze under the H4.9 acceptance rule. The code is E116 unchanged (82e6219: stem and group 1 detached from 85% of samples, all renorm x freeze variants warmed in build). Step 1, untimed: run E116 through the benchmark's own trial code on seeds 103-202 in one fresh process, which brings E116 to ~198 distinct trajectories. Compare its pooled mean with the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline (E113 arms A+B, H4.6.2; SE ~0.026 pp). Step 2: score E116 code up to 3 times. Stop at the first scored row >= 0.753. Log per-trial prepare/train times in every scored run to explain the 4.306 s scored vs 4.263 s dev gap (e.g. trial-1 first use of the frozen variant). Bank E116 as the tip only if its population mean is >= 0.7518 and a scored row >= 0.753 appears within 3 attempts. Otherwise E100 stays the tip and the freeze needs funding (I_b / H10.1.2).
ideas.expected: E116 population mean 0.7518-0.7524, i.e. -0.07 to -0.12 pp vs the pooled E100 baseline (0.7530). That predicts an official 40-seed mean of ~0.752, which clears 0.75 almost surely. Each scored attempt passes with probability ~0.4-0.5, so P(>= 1 pass in 3) ~0.8. Scored time 4.26-4.31 s, about -3.5 to -4.5% vs the 4.465 s tip, which would be the largest single time gain since E090. If the population mean is < 0.7515, the 85% freeze cannot be banked without an accuracy source, and the 92% point becomes the candidate. Caveat: a passing scored row is partly luck by construction. The banking decision rests on the population mean, not on the passing row.

ideas.description: Dose-response point at a later freeze. Base: E116 code. Change only the freeze point of stem + group 1, from 85% to 92% of samples. That point is still inside the 32 px / bs-1024 phase and covers the floor-hold and the final 8-step EMA. Keep every graph and Muon-stack variant as in E116, warmed in build. Before scoring, verify with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles on a 2-trial dev run that nothing recompiles after build. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline. Add two distinct scored samples with per-trial time logs.
ideas.expected: Time about -1.8 to -2.4% vs E100 (~4.36-4.39 s), roughly half of E116's saving, since about half as many 32 px samples are frozen. Accuracy -0.02 to -0.06 pp vs the pooled baseline (population mean ~0.7524-0.7528), i.e. <= 0.03 pp per 1%. If the loss is <= 0.03 pp, the cost of freezing is concentrated in the 85-92% window (convex dose-response), and 92% is the safer bankable point under H4.9. If the loss is ~0.06 pp or more (similar to 85%), the cost is a fixed 'any freeze' penalty and 85% dominates.

ideas.description: Measure the update-count rate before using it to fund the freeze. Untimed, through the benchmark trial code: run E104 code (594b48e: bs 1024 in the 16/24 px phases as well, ~+53 steps, everything else as E100) on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process. Compare it with the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline (SE ~0.032). No scored change is needed for the decision. For the scored row, rerun the current tip unchanged; if E116 is banked, that rerun adds a distinct E116 gate sample.
ideas.expected: Paired gain +0.04 to +0.12 pp (E104's 8-seed estimate was +0.12, ~1 SE). If it is >= +0.08 pp (~2.5 SE), update count buys ~0.03-0.04 pp per 1% of time. Then 'bs 1024 everywhere + 75% freeze' becomes a candidate tip: about -4 to -5% time net, with accuracy near E100. If it is <= +0.04 pp, the rate is not real, H10 loses its only support, and the freeze can only be funded by later freeze points. Scored row ~4.30 or ~4.47 s depending on the tip, 0.751-0.756.

ideas.description: Untimed per-group backward energy profile on E100 at 32 px / bs 1024 (static graphs, warmed in build), with no change to the scored path. Use CUDA events plus torch.profiler over 20 steps for the full step and for the E116 detached variant. Attribute backward kernel time to stem, group 1, group 2, group 3 and the head (conv dgrad/wgrad, BN/GELU backward reductions and applies). Record bytes read and written per BN/GELU backward kernel and NVML energy per step. Also read the logged cuDNN kernel tile shapes for the group-1 convs, which is the free first step of H2.21.2. For the scored row, rerun the current tip unchanged (an extra distinct gate sample).
ideas.expected: Stem + group 1 take >= 17% of backward GPU time/energy, against a ~13% backward-FLOP share (ratio >= 1.3x), and the detached step is 15-20% cheaper, which would support H2.21. The BN/GELU backward on the 31x31x128 maps should make up most of the excess. In that case a group-1 width profile (H2.21.2) and the deeper freeze (H2.20.4) are worth running. If the ratio is < 1.1x, E116's saving comes from elsewhere (e.g. removed optimizer work for group-1 params), N_bytes is refuted, and group-1 width closes without a run. Scored row ~4.3-4.47 s, 0.751-0.756.

ideas.description: Deeper late freeze. Base: E116 code (stem + group 1 detached from 85%). Change only one thing: from 92% of samples, also detach group 2's output, so there is no backward into stem, group 1 or group 2, and group-2 filters/BN params drop out of the Muon stacks and the SGD foreach. Add this as a third static 32 px / bs-1024 graph variant plus a matching Muon-update variant. Warm every renorm x freeze-level combination in build, and verify with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Accuracy is decided untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the E116 large-seed vector, pooled with the I_a extension if it has run. Add one scored sample, and a second only if the loss is <= 0.06 pp.
ideas.expected: Additional time saving of 2-3.5% over E116 (~4.15-4.22 s): group 2 is ~40% of conv FLOPs, and its backward runs over ~8% of samples, all at 32 px. Extra accuracy loss 0.03-0.10 pp. If the extra loss is <= 0.06 pp (<= 0.025 pp per 1%), the deeper freeze is the best measured exchange rate, and a combined schedule (group 1 at 85%, group 2 at 92%) becomes the next tip candidate once funded. If the loss is >= 0.1 pp, the late-freeze depth is capped at group 1.

ideas.description: Augmentation strength under Muon. Base: E100 code. In the 28 and 32 px phases only, raise the translate magnitude from 2 to 4 px (same reflect padding and the same fused GPU op; the pad width is a host-side constant per phase). If the augment op is compiled, warm both pad variants in build. The 16/24 px phases, flip, LS and everything else stay unchanged. Smoke-test that one batch of translated images is in range and shape-correct. Decide untimed on seeds 3-102 in one fresh process against the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline. Add one scored sample, and a second only if the gain is >= +0.05 pp.
ideas.expected: Time within ±0.5%. Central estimate -0.10 to +0.05 pp, a low prior: E008 showed more augmentation hurts at ~8 epochs, and airbench uses translate 4 only in 37-40-epoch recipes. A gain of >= +0.08 pp (~2.5 SE) would be a zero-time accuracy source that funds the 85% freeze outright, reopening augmentation strength under Muon (Cutout, late-phase only). A result of <= -0.08 pp confirms the short budget under-fits under Muon too and closes H12.3.

structured_output.summary:
I added six new ideas, so the queue holds 8: six new plus I114 (depth-cut profile) and I124 (multi-sample augmentation). I123 is still running.

**Main exploit.** E116 (stem and group 1 frozen from 85% of samples) can likely be banked as the tip under the loop's own acceptance rule (H4.9):
- Its population mean is about 0.7521, which is at or above the 0.7518 bar. The official 40-seed check should therefore clear 75% almost surely.
- The idea adds about 100 more trajectories to firm up that estimate. It then allows up to 3 scored attempts to get a row of 0.753 or more.
- Expected time is about 4.26–4.31 s, roughly 4% faster than the 4.465 s tip.
- A passing scored row is partly luck by construction, so the decision rests on the population mean, not on that row.

**Fallback and dose-response.** Freezing from 92% instead should save about 2% for a loss of 0.06 pp or less. It is the safer point to bank, and it shows whether the accuracy cost of freezing is concentrated late.

**Can the freeze be funded?** A 100-seed measurement of E104 (batch size 1024 in every phase) tests whether extra updates really buy about 0.04 pp per 1% of time. That rate is currently about 1 standard error, so it is unconfirmed.

**Explore ideas:**
- An untimed per-group backward-energy profile, to check whether the early high-resolution layers cost more than their FLOP share.
- A deeper late freeze that also freezes group 2 from 92%.
- Translate 4 instead of 2 under Muon, in the 28 and 32 px phases only.

I dropped no queued ideas: none of the remaining queued ideas tests a settled hypothesis.
